message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo, and their phenotyping_reported fields indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm endpoints (one explicitly prevalent). Several candidates come from pan-trait/framework/portability contexts (PGS001784: Global Biobank lessons; PGS002054: UKB portability of 245 scores), and others are disease-focused (PGS000753: AAA architecture in MVP; PGS003972/PGS003973: AAA GWAS meta-analysis in Nat Genet; PGS003429: AAA screening/cost-effectiveness). Comparable PRS-only discrimination is largely missing across the set; where AUROC/C-index is reported it is generally full-model and/or covariate-dependent (e.g., PGS001784 AUROC=0.868 with extensive age/sex interactions and PCs; PGS003973 C-index=0.882 with age/age^2/sex), so it cannot be treated as PRS-only superiority per the provided domain rules. PGS000753 is selected as a conservative best-supported direct-match because it is clearly AAA-focused, uses basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), reports a per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) supporting nontrivial PRS signal, and has reasonably sized validation (n=46,564) without relying on a framework-paper metric advantage. The main limitation is unresolved competition from the newer, disease-focused Nat Genet models (PGS003972/PGS003973) which may be stronger but are difficult to rank here because their reported discrimination appears to be full-model (and is not PRS-isolated) and covariates are unknown for one; hence low confidence and a sub-optimal direct-match outcome."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is prevalent AAA). Among them, PGS003972 (PRS-CS; Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis) is supported by a disease-focused, multi-cohort development context (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) rather than a pan-trait/portability framework (PGS001784, PGS002054) or an older sparse P+T score (PGS000753). However, the visible performance evidence is hard to compare because several candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index and/or have missing PRS-only metrics; notably PGS003973 shows a very high C-index (0.882) but it is a full model with covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) and no PRS-only/incremental metric, so it cannot be treated as stronger PRS discrimination than PGS003972. Between the two Nat Genet PRS-CS scores (PGS003972 AUROC=0.69 vs PGS003973 C-index=0.882), the metrics are not clearly comparable and other key fields (e.g., covariates for PGS003972 are unknown; validation sizes are small and similar), leaving unresolved conflict; therefore selection is low-confidence and overall outcome is sub-optimal despite presence of direct matches."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent). The strongest disease-focused evidence in this set comes from the dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis paper (Nat Genet, 2023) that yields two PRS-CS scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) developed across many AAA-relevant cohorts, which domain_knowledge indicates should generally outrank pan-trait/portability framework scores when endpoint fidelity is comparable. Between the two Nat Genet scores, PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) but it is not a PRS-only metric and includes age/age^2/sex covariates; PGS003972 reports a lower full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates. Given domain guidance not to substitute full-model discrimination for PRS-only performance and to treat unknown covariates as a confidence penalty, the evidence does not cleanly separate them; however PGS003972 avoids the visibly covariate-including packaging and therefore is the slightly cleaner PRS candidate in the limited metadata. Overall confidence is low because PRS-only AUROC/PGS-only R2 are largely missing across the leading disease-focused candidates, and the apparently strong full-model metrics (including 0.882) may be largely covariate-driven rather than PRS-driven."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct phenotype matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). Several higher-variant, newer models exist (PGS003972/PGS003973 from a disease-focused Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis; PGS003429 from a screening/cost-effectiveness paper), but their visible discrimination metrics are full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown or basic covariates and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 reported, making cross-model comparison ambiguous. Two framework-style scores (PGS001784: ‘Global Biobank analyses…’; PGS002054: ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores…’) provide PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only R2≈0.0147; partial-r≈0.0144) but domain guidance down-ranks portability/pan-trait frameworks when disease-focused alternatives exist, and their main reported AUROC values appear full-model. PGS000753 is from an AAA-focused MVP/Mayo study and reports a clear per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, European validation), with basic covariates and a moderate validation size; however, it is sparse (29 variants), uses a prevalent endpoint, and lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, so it is selected only as the most coherent disease-focused option given the limited, non-comparable performance reporting across the set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches with aligned endpoint labels (all report abdominal aortic aneurysm; phenotyping_reported is AAA, with PGS000753 explicitly prevalent AAA). Several candidates come from pan-trait/framework/portability-style publications (PGS001784: Global Biobank lessons; PGS002054: Portability of 245 scores), which domain guidance down-ranks when disease-focused alternatives exist. Among the remaining more disease-focused options, PGS000753 (MVP AAA genetic architecture study) provides the clearest PRS-specific signal via an effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates and reasonable validation size; competing recent disease-focused models (PGS003972/PGS003973 from a Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis) report only full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) without explicit PRS-only metrics in the provided context and include unknown/limited covariate details, making cross-model PRS comparability unclear. Because most candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 (and the highest reported AUCs appear to be full-model/covariate-influenced rather than isolated PRS performance), the evidence is insufficient to confidently select a single clearly best model, so the choice remains low-confidence and thus sub-optimal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). Two candidates (PGS001784, PGS002054) come from identified pan-trait/framework/portability papers (Global Biobank lessons; UKB portability of 245 PGS), and their prominent reported metrics include PRS-only R2/partial-r that are modest and do not clearly dominate; their very large validation sizes therefore should not outweigh disease-focused evidence per the provided policy. Among the disease-focused options, PGS000753 (Million Veteran Program AAA genetics paper) has clean/basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), an explicit per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), and multi-ancestry evaluation context, making it a solid, coherent direct-match package. Competing newer disease-focused scores (PGS003972/PGS003973 from a Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis; PGS003429 Nat Commun screening/cost-effectiveness paper) report only full-model AUROC/C-index with missing PRS-only metrics and/or unknown covariates, reducing comparability and making it unclear whether their higher discrimination is PRS-driven. Because key PRS-comparable performance metrics are missing or non-comparable across several candidates, the selection is supported but not definitive, hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL with moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned). Among them, PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis publication context (Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with broad multi-cohort development, and reports a full-model AUROC (0.69) under European evaluation—providing some performance support without relying on an identified risk-wrapper or biomarker-heavy covariates (covariates are listed as Unknown rather than explicitly clinical). Limitations: key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC / incremental AUROC) are not reported for most models; several competing candidates are framework/portability scores with explicit PRS-side metrics and/or much larger validation (e.g., PGS001784 with PGS-only R2=0.014661; PGS002054 partial-r=0.0144), making the evidence mixed and not sufficient for a clearly high-quality single winner. Additionally, PGS003973 shows very high C-index (0.882) but it is a full-model metric with age/age^2/sex covariates and is not directly comparable as PRS-only performance, so it cannot dominate the ranking."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All six candidates are direct matches with aligned disease endpoints (phenotyping_reported is abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS002054 and PGS001784) come from explicit portability/framework-style papers, which domain guidance says to down-rank when disease-focused alternatives exist, even if they report PRS-comparable metrics (partial-r or covariates-regressed-out R2). Among the remaining disease-focused options, the Nat Genet GWAS meta-analysis models (PGS003972/PGS003973) have the strongest disease-specific multi-cohort development context; between them, PGS003972 is preferred because it reports a PRS-side discrimination metric (AUROC=0.69) without the extra uncertainty introduced by the very high full-model C-index in PGS003973, which is not PRS-only and could be largely covariate-driven. Key limitation: across candidates, PRS-only AUROC is generally missing and several reported AUROC/C-index values appear to be full-model metrics; covariates are unknown for some models, so comparability is imperfect and lowers confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo and report an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) endpoint. Two models (PGS003972, PGS003973) come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis publication (Nat Genet, 2023) with large multi-cohort development (many contributing cohorts) and European evaluation, which domain guidance prioritizes over pan-trait/framework portability scores. Between these, PGS003972 has the cleanest/most generic PRS framing in the visible metadata (no explicit clinical-covariate augmentation disclosed; covariates listed as Unknown) and is a straightforward AAA diagnosis endpoint; its reported AUROC (0.69) is modest but avoids the interpretability risk that PGS003973’s very high full-model C-index (0.882) could be largely covariate-driven (it explicitly includes Age, Age^2, Sex), and no PRS-only/incremental metric is shown to attribute that discrimination to the PRS. Competing framework-style models (PGS001784 global biobank PRS-CS-auto; PGS002054 UKB portability LDpred2) and a screening/cost-effectiveness oriented paper score (PGS003429) are down-ranked per domain rules when a disease-focused multi-cohort alternative exists, especially since their reported metrics are not clearly PRS-only comparable (often full-model AUROC/partial-r) and can be covariate-driven. Remaining limitation: the catalog lacks PRS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC for the leading disease-focused models, and covariates are unknown for PGS003972, so the choice is supported mainly by study archetype/endpoint fidelity rather than directly comparable PRS-only performance."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still endpoint-faithful). Two candidates (PGS001784, PGS002054) come from pan-trait/portability framework-style papers, which domain guidance says should generally not outrank disease-focused models unless they have clearly stronger endpoint+metric evidence; additionally, their reported metrics are limited in PRS-isolated comparability (e.g., partial-r=0.0144 for PGS002054; PGS-only R2=0.014661 for PGS001784, with full-model AUROC likely largely covariate-driven).
